newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesia palm olein edges up in late trade.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia palm olein edges up in late trade.

text.p: Indonesian palm olein prices were slightly higher in late trading on Tuesday on sustained steady demand, traders said.
They said palm olein was quoted at 1,410 rupiah/kg in Jakarta, up from 1,405-10 rupiah at the opening, but offers were also heard at 1,415 rupiah.
The traders said crude palm oil was done at 1,239 rupiah/kg at a tender in the North Sumatran city of Medan, while at another tender it was sold at 1,244 rupiah.
"The market is picking up, with demand coming in after a long lull," one trader said.
Traders also said crop data released by the Malaysian Palm Oil Registration and Licensing Authority (PORLA) was market friendly, with stocks declining and exports rising.

PORLA said Malaysian crude palm oil output rose 35.71 percent to 683,196 tonnes in March from 503,415 in February. It said March palm oil exports rose to 565,219 tonnes from 380,267 tonnes in February, while stocks fell to 689,633 tonnes at end-March from 723,399 tonnes at end-February.
"I think the data will help firm the market in the near term," one trader said. "The Malaysian market was a victim of profit taking today."
